# PV101 CTS Cohort 6 Day 2 - 2026-07-07

**Topic:** Electricity Basics, Multimeter Practice, Series and Parallel  
**Source note:** Generated in ChatGPT from Tim Milkewicz CTS/PV101 context, with Dropbox reference PV101_Common_Solar_Terms_and_Equations_Print_Ready_2026-03-24.pdf used for terms/equation alignment.

## Architecture of the Day

- Theme: Solar is not magic. It is light becoming electrical behavior that we can measure, predict, and respect.
- Core idea: Before students install parts, they need to understand what the system is trying to do.
- Assessment: Meter practice sheet, quiz, labeled circuit/system sketch, and exit ticket.

## Learning Targets

- Students explain voltage, current, resistance, and power in simple language.
- Students identify the difference between AC and DC.
- Students use a multimeter to safely measure DC voltage.
- Students explain why PV modules can be energized when exposed to light.
- Students predict what changes in series and parallel connections.
- Students connect the basics to the Cohort 6 RV solar capstone.

## Instructor Day Flow

| Time | Block | Instructor Action |
|---|---|---|
| 10:00-10:15 | Arrival reset | Green/yellow/red check-in. Set a calm safety tone. Board: Solar work rewards patience. Guessing is not a method. |
| 10:15-10:35 | Day 1 review | PV = photovoltaic. Photo = light. Voltaic = electricity/voltage. Connect review to the RV solar capstone. |
| 10:35-11:05 | Electricity basics | Teach voltage, current, resistance, power, and Watts = Volts x Amps. Keep it concrete and example-based. |
| 11:05-11:20 | AC vs DC | Solar panels and batteries are DC. Homes and many appliances are AC. Inverters translate DC to AC. |
| 11:20-11:30 | Break | Move bodies. Reset attention. |
| 11:30-12:05 | Multimeter practice | Inspect leads, set meter, measure batteries and low-voltage sources. Do not freestyle current measurement. |
| 12:05-12:30 | PV light demo | Measure panel voltage in light, shade, tilted, and covered conditions. Have students predict first. |
| 12:30-1:00 | Lunch | Clean table reset before leaving. |
| 1:00-1:35 | Series and parallel | Series stacks voltage. Parallel stacks amperage. Use math examples. |
| 1:35-2:10 | Mini-build or circuit trace | Source -> fuse -> switch -> load -> return. Students label current path and test points. |
| 2:10-2:25 | RV capstone bridge | Start the load list. AC/DC, voltage, watts/amps, hours per day, notes. |
| 2:25-2:45 | Quiz | 10-question Day 2 quiz. |
| 2:45-2:55 | Exit ticket | Understanding, practice need, safety rule, RV load to verify. |
| 2:55-3:00 | Cleanup | Meters off, leads wrapped, tools returned, batteries stored, papers collected. |

## Board Notes

| Term | Plain Meaning |
|---|---|
| PV | Photovoltaic: photo = light, voltaic = electricity/voltage. |
| Voltage | Electrical pressure. Unit: volts (V). |
| Current | Electrical flow. Unit: amps (A). |
| Resistance | Opposition to flow. Unit: ohms. |
| Power | Work being done. Unit: watts (W). |
| Formula | Watts = Volts x Amps |
| DC | Direct current. One direction. Solar panels and batteries. |
| AC | Alternating current. Changes direction. Wall outlets and many appliances. |
| Series | Voltage adds. Current stays about the same. |
| Parallel | Current adds. Voltage stays about the same. |

## Multimeter Safety Rules

1. Inspect the meter and leads before use.
2. Set the meter before touching the circuit.
3. Black lead goes in COM.
4. Red lead goes in the correct port for the measurement.
5. Voltage is measured across two points.
6. Current is measured in series, not across a battery.
7. Never short a battery with meter leads.
8. If unsure, stop and ask.

## Student Handout Sections

### Big Idea
- Solar PV turns light into DC electricity. We use measurements instead of guesses.
### Electricity Words
- Voltage = pressure
- Current = flow
- Resistance = opposition
- Power = work being done
### Units
- Voltage = volts = V
- Current = amps = A
- Resistance = ohms
- Power = watts = W
### Main Formula
- Watts = Volts x Amps
- Amps = Watts / Volts
- Volts = Watts / Amps
### AC vs DC
- DC = direct current: batteries, solar panels, many RV loads
- AC = alternating current: wall outlets and many home appliances
### Series and Parallel
- Series = voltage adds
- Parallel = current adds
- Memory line: Series stacks voltage. Parallel stacks amperage.
### PV System Path
- Solar panel -> charge controller -> battery -> loads
- Battery -> inverter -> AC loads when needed

PV101 Day 2 - Electricity Basics + Meter Practice

Today we covered the foundation needed for solar work: voltage, current, resistance, watts, AC vs DC, safe multimeter use, and the difference between series and parallel wiring.

Main idea:
Solar panels produce DC electricity when exposed to light.
Voltage pushes.
Current flows.
Resistance limits.
Power does work.
Watts = Volts x Amps.
